transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you. Um... I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess what brings me in is that my... well, my eating has just gotten a little off lately. It's probably not a huge deal, honestly, but some days I barely get down a coffee and a granola bar before a shift. I just haven't had much of an appetite. And, um, I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose on me lately, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. Is... is that the kind of thing I should be coming in for? I just wanted to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.
Beyond your appetite, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or uninterested in things you usually enjoy?

Um, well... I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, especially for the patients, you know? I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining... but I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been a little tough lately. 

Most mornings, I wake up with this... this really heavy, hollow feeling. It kind of feels like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. I always try to just push through it, I promise. Does that make sense? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let me think... I really hope I'm giving you the right timeline here. I don't want to mislead you or anything. But, um, I guess this steady kind of sadness... and just not caring about things as much... it really settled in later on. 

If I had to put a number on it, I'd say it's been with me for roughly the past year and four months or so. Give or take a little? I always try to tell myself it'll pass, and I really do try to snap out of it. Is... is it normal for it to last that long? I hope I'm not doing something wrong to make it stick around.
During these past sixteen months, have there been any periods where you felt significantly worse than you do now, or has your mood been consistently at this same level?

Um... I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to. I really don't want to sound like I'm whining or anything, because I know people have it so much worse. But, um... I guess it's been pretty consistent. 

It's not just, like, a few bad weeks here and there where I feel extra down. For most of this whole stretch—the last year and four months—I've just been living with that same heavy, hollow mood and not really caring about things. I try my best to hide it at work, I really do. But it's just kind of... always there in the background. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Beyond the change in your appetite, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns, such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much?

Um, well... I try not to let it affect my job, you know? I know how important it is to be well-rested for the patients. But, um... I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. I hope that's okay to admit.

It's just... I get into bed and my mind just keeps replaying everything from work, and I find myself just lying there, listening for every little noise. So my sleep gets kind of broken up. And then, usually around 3 or 4 in the morning, I just wake up completely. I really try to go back to sleep, I promise I do, but I just can't seem to settle back down before my alarm goes off. Is... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I just want to be honest with you.

During these past sixteen months, have there ever been any two-week periods where your mood felt significantly deeper or more severe than this constant baseline, and you also experienced a cluster of other symptoms like feeling worthless or having trouble concentrating?

Um... I really hope I'm not complaining too much. I know everyone has bad days, and I definitely don't want to sound like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. But... I guess there have been times, yeah, where it gets a lot heavier. 

I just... I start feeling really guilty, I suppose? Like, I keep thinking I'm just this huge burden to the clinic, and to my family. And I know I shouldn't think that way, I really try to be positive. But if I make even a tiny mistake at work—like, if I'm a little slow turning over a room for the next patient—I just beat myself up over it so badly. It feels like I've ruined everyone's entire day, even though I know logically that's probably an overreaction. 

I hope it's okay that I'm sharing that. I just... I feel so worthless when it gets like that. Does that make sense? I'm trying to give you the right kind of examples.
When you have these periods where you feel especially worthless or guilty, how long do those specific, more intense episodes typically last?

Um... I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm keeping track of every bad day, because I really try to just push through them. I know the clinic needs me, and I don't want to let anyone down. But, um... to answer your question... I guess I'm not exactly sure how long they last. 

It's hard to put a strict timeline on it, you know? Sometimes it feels like those really heavy feelings stick around for a while, but I try so hard to just keep smiling and doing my job that the days kind of blur together. I haven't really marked it on a calendar or anything. I hope that's an okay answer? I'm sorry I don't have a more exact number of days or weeks for you. I just try to focus on being helpful and getting past it.
When you have those times where you feel especially worthless or guilty, do those feelings usually stick around for at least two weeks at a time?

Um... well, I really try not to let it drag on that long, if I can help it. I know I have to be there for the patients, so I try to just shake it off, you know? But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, and I really want to be honest with you... sometimes it probably does last a couple of weeks. 

I just try so hard to hide it at work, so maybe it doesn't seem like it's been that long to anyone else. But inside, yeah, I suppose those really heavy, guilty feelings can hang on for two weeks, maybe even a little longer sometimes. I hope I'm not making it sound like I just give up, because I really do try to fight it. Is... is that the kind of timeline you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

You mentioned that these heavier, more intense periods of feeling worthless can last for at least two weeks; have you experienced more than one of these distinct, two-week-long episodes since you started feeling this way sixteen months ago?

Um... I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm constantly falling apart, because I really do try to keep things together. But... yeah, I guess there's been more than one of those two-week stretches where it gets really bad. 

But I want to be clear, I'm not just, you know, having a couple of bad weeks and then feeling totally fine. I don't want you to think I'm exaggerating. It's more like... for most of this whole sixteen months, I've just been living with this really heavy, hollow feeling. And I just don't have much interest in things most of the time. It's just kind of always there in the background, even when it's not one of those really intense two-week periods. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture without sounding like a complainer. Am I explaining that right?
Looking back at the last sixteen months, has there ever been a stretch of two months or more where you felt completely like your old self, free from this constant heavy, hollow feeling?

Um... well, no, not completely free from it, I guess. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm never doing well! There was actually a time—maybe a few months ago—where my mood did lift quite a bit. I even started running a little again, just trying to stay healthy, you know? And getting through the work day felt a lot easier. I was really trying my best to get back to normal.

But... um... even during that time, when my mood was better, I still wasn't totally... myself. I hope it's okay to mention this, but for several weeks during that better period, I was still... well, I was still hearing those comments when I was alone in the hallways at the clinic. And I was still looking at the staff schedule because it felt like there were hidden warnings in it about me. 

So, I guess my mood was better, but those other things were still happening. I'm sorry, I hope that's not too confusing? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right, but I also want you to know I really was trying to do better during that time. Did that answer what you were asking?

When you hear those comments in the hallways or see those warnings in the staff schedule, do you feel like those things are actually happening to you, or do you sometimes wonder if they might just be in your head?

Um... well... I know how it sounds, and I really don't want you to think I'm just making things up or being paranoid. I try to be a good employee, I really do. But... when I see those things in the schedule, it feels so real to me. 

Like... I keep getting stuck on this idea that certain people at the clinic are watching my charting times, you know? And I feel like they're leaving these little signs in the staff schedule to show they're building a case against me. My supervisor tells me it's just the new workflow, and I really try to believe her, I do! I don't want to cause any trouble. 

But... it's just so hard to shake the feeling that it's actually happening. Even when I try to tell myself it might just be in my head, the feeling that they're watching me is just so strong. I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything? I'm really trying to be logical about it, but it's just... it's really hard. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

patient.answer:
Um... well, no, not completely free from it, I guess. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm never doing well! There was actually a time—maybe a few months ago—where my mood did lift quite a bit. I even started running a little again, just trying to stay healthy, you know? And getting through the work day felt a lot easier. I was really trying my best to get back to normal.

But... um... even during that time, when my mood was better, I still wasn't totally... myself. I hope it's okay to mention this, but for several weeks during that better period, I was still... well, I was still hearing those comments when I was alone in the hallways at the clinic. And I was still looking at the staff schedule because it felt like there were hidden warnings in it about me. 

So, I guess my mood was better, but those other things were still happening. I'm sorry, I hope that's not too confusing? I just want to make sure I'm answering you right, but I also want you to know I really was trying to do better during that time. Did that answer what you were asking?

inference.note: The patient's report of experiencing auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions (hidden warnings in the schedule) even during periods of improved mood necessitates the inclusion of a psychotic disorder differential, moving beyond simple mood disorders.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's experiences of hearing voices and interpreting the schedule as having hidden warnings are related to a specific belief system or are isolated occurrences, to differentiate between F22 (Delusional Disorder) and F34.1 (Persistent Depressive Disorder with psychotic features).
doctor.question: When you hear those comments in the hallways or see those warnings in the staff schedule, do you feel like those things are actually happening to you, or do you sometimes wonder if they might just be in your head?

target_item.name: Delusions

patient.answer:
Um... well... I know how it sounds, and I really don't want you to think I'm just making things up or being paranoid. I try to be a good employee, I really do. But... when I see those things in the schedule, it feels so real to me. 

Like... I keep getting stuck on this idea that certain people at the clinic are watching my charting times, you know? And I feel like they're leaving these little signs in the staff schedule to show they're building a case against me. My supervisor tells me it's just the new workflow, and I really try to believe her, I do! I don't want to cause any trouble. 

But... it's just so hard to shake the feeling that it's actually happening. Even when I try to tell myself it might just be in my head, the feeling that they're watching me is just so strong. I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything? I'm really trying to be logical about it, but it's just... it's really hard. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.

inference.note: The patient describes a chronic mood disturbance (consistent with persistent depressive disorder) that has persisted for 16 months, accompanied by clear psychotic symptoms (delusions of being watched/monitored and auditory hallucinations) that persist even when the mood symptoms improve. This combination of symptoms occurring concurrently for a significant period points towards Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
